steps.text: Place potatoes in a large pot of lightly salted water. Bring to a boil and cook until tender, about 15 minutes; drain.
Transfer potatoes into a large bowl and mash.
Stir in sour cream, cream cheese, milk, onion salt, and pepper until well combined.
Transfer into a large casserole dish. Let potatoes cool completely, 15 to 20 minutes. Cover with aluminum foil and refrigerate for up to 2 days.
When ready to bake, remove casserole from the refrigerator and let sit for 30 minutes on the counter. Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C).
Bake, covered, in the preheated oven for 50 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Make-Ahead Mashed Potatoes
raw_recipe.description: These make-ahead mashed potatoes are deliciously rich thanks to the addition of cream cheese and sour cream. Simply heat through when ready to serve!

review.reviewBody: This is a GREAT time saver for a busy holiday. I make ahead then throw in the crockpot on low the morning of the holiday so that I save oven space and they're ready to eat by the time the rest of the dinner's done. I've had several requests for this recipe. Also really good using redskin potatoes!
We have made this for many holiday dinners. You can also put these in a crockpot for 5 to 6 hours. It's a great way to keep them warm without the hassle of watching over them!

So good and what a blessing to make ahead! I threw in 3-4 cloves of garlic with the potatoes to boil and mashed them right with the taters. Also added about 1/2 cup grated parmesan, and sprinkled top with paprika for color.

I served these potatoes as a side to beef tenderloin for Christmas Eve dinner, and they got rave reviews. After mashing the potatoes and adding all the ingredients, I placed everything in a buttered crock pot and refrigerated it over night. The next morning, all I had to do was plug in the slow cooker and set to low. Simple and absolutely delicious! (I skipped the baking step.)

I have made these and everyone loves them. The only difference instead of onion powder I use chopped onions. I saute the onions in butter and add that to the mix. Great flavor. I put in the crock pot to reheat. Put a towel between the pot and the lid in the crockpot to catch all the steam/water so you don't water them down.

I make these months in advance. Up to 6 months. Put them in the freezer in a vacuum pack bag. Thawed them out Day of and baked them with cheese on them. Everyone loved them and I'm not standing on my feet all day. Win for everyone! I do add chives or herbs depending on what I am serving them with. My husband doesn't like gravy so we melt some cheese and some times bacon bits on top at the end of baking.

Great. Don't overcook the potatoes, or it will be difficult to separate them from the water. Mine were a bit wet, so I baked the finished casserole in the oven without a lid, to dry then out a bit. I used a stand mixer to thoroughly mix the sour cream, cream cheese, and 1/2 cup butter. Then I manually mashed and stirred in the potatoes. Don't mix the potatoes with the mixer, as that produces too much gluten and will make the potatoes sticky/stretchy. I did not add milk, having used butter instead. I was in a rush and timed myself, starting from nonwashed whole potatoes to ready to serve dish, did take a full 1hr 20 min. I did not peel my red potatoes.

My husband was so nervous about this recipe! He really likes his mashed potatoes and thought I would ruin Thanksgiving dinner with a preposterous make ahead mashed potato recipe :)........He and everyone else loved them. After reading reviewers recommendations, I made the recipe as is, put them in a crock pot on low 2 hours before dinner, put a stick of butter on top to melt 30 minutes before serving. This recipe was a great time saver on a hectic Holiday morning. I will definitely make this again for special occasions. Thanks so much! Update 11/29/2025 - this recipe is a keeper. I have made this every single Thanksgiving since 2014. One less thing to worry about the day of and we all love it!

Made for the first time yesterday for Christmas. This is a keeper. Halfed the recipe. Added garlic to the potatoes as they boiled, then mashed the garlic with the potatoes. Made them a day ahead . Didn’t bake in oven. Placed in slow cooker at low setting and from time to time added a little milk. Came out wonderfully creamy. Great recipe.

Use 8 ounces cream cheese and skip the milk. Half the sour cream. Regular salt and pepper. Add a whole stick of butter! Whip smooth with a mixer. The milk makes them runny. Plain salt only, no onion salt. Whip smooth, put them in the crock of your large crockpot. Put lid on and store in fridge. When ready to use, heat in crock pot. No lumpy mashed potatoes for me, I don't see the point in mashed potatoes if they're full of lumps. Also, I prefer red potatoes. Better flavor.

Excellent recipe! I only used 1 (8 oz) brick of cream cheese and added minced garlic. I didn't have any onion powder but I did add some chopped, fresh chives instead. Very creamy and delicious. I also had about a 1/2 cup of chicken broth that I was looking to get rid of and rather than pouring it down the sink, I added it to the potatoes. I made the morning of Thanksgiving and put into a crock pot and kept in the refrigerator until about 4 hours before we are planning to eat.
I make these every Christmas or Thanksgiving. They are a huge hit with the family. I tend to go with make ahead recipes for big celebrations so I can enjoy the day and family as well.

This is a favourite in our house. I like how the potatoes can be made ahead of time and still taste like freshly mashed potatoes. I worked a banquet where there were a lot of mashed potatoes left and the caterer was going to toss them. I said I would take them and I mixed them up with this recipe. It made a few casseroles so I froze them to see if that would work. After thawing and baking them they were as delicious as if they had been freshly made. This is a great way to use up leftover mashed potatoes instead of tossing them out and a very handy side dish to have in the freezer.

Amazing!! Made these for thanksgiving to save myself some time on thanksgiving day and they were delicious! I misread the recipe and used 1 - 8 oz package of cream cheese. Definitely making this again. The entire family loved them and raved about the recipe even my husband who was not happy I was making them ahead of time. In the picture there is bitter butter but that was not listed in the recipe.
Good taste and makes a lot of potatoes. I cooked them the day before and then put in a crockpot on low for a couple hours to warm through before our gathering,

My MIL made these for years and gave me the recipe. I, too, have been making them for years. A couple of years ago I was working a few days before Thanksgiving and my husband and daughter were home. They decided they would help out and prepare the mashed potatoes. They thought the 2, 3 ounce packages of cream cheese was a typo and added 2, 8 ounce packages. As good as the original is, this was even better and we’ve been making it that was ever since.

This recipe is very similar to one I have used since the late 90s. It is wonderful because it works great when you need to take a dish or want to make your potatoes a day ahead. I then put the potatoes in a crockpot and warm them. It also warms up well in the microwave. We always called it company potatoes.
*NOTE THE USE OF ONLY 6 oz. Cream cheese. WHO BUYS CREAM CHEESE IN A 3 OZ. CONTAINER?! My fault for not reading more closely. I hope I haven’t ruined these.
I used all vegan ingedience
These tasted like eating Sour Cream and Onion Potato Chips—not like mashed potatoes. I really don’t like them.
